battle.name: 第一次卡洛斯戰爭
battle.theater: 納瓦拉、巴斯克山區與馬埃斯特拉戈
battle.brief: 一八三三年九月費爾南多七世病逝，十月卡洛斯在維多利亞宣布為王，王位爭議在西班牙引爆卡洛斯內戰，戰火燒遍納瓦拉、巴斯克山區與馬埃斯特拉戈，打了六年九個月。卡面的輪發槍是最早的後膛手槍，一八三三年只剩軍官與衛兵手上還有它；決定勝負的，是步槍、炮兵、山徑與車隊。

kit.name: 輪發槍
kit.history: 最早的後膛手槍。機械太貴，只給火槍隊的軍官與衛兵。

countries: 交戰的兩方是卡洛斯派與自由派。卡洛斯派以已故費爾南多七世之弟卡洛斯·德·波旁為王位正統，北方以「十萬人」為號，在納瓦拉、巴斯克三省、阿拉貢與加泰隆尼亞的抵抗運動裡迅速成軍：基層是教區神甫與本堂區牧人，核心是熟悉海岸與山徑的漁民、走私者與農莊武裝，骨幹軍官多出自由派軍中倒戈的步兵軍官與老兵，編制沿用舊式營連，輔以各村的游擊小組，稱為「神甫的祝福」。東線由卡布雷拉與莫雷亞伯爵率領，獨立在巴倫西亞與卡塔隆尼亞內陸活動。北方的傳統主義支持者集中在巴斯克與納瓦拉的農村，以「福爾羅斯」（地方舊憲法特權）與天主教會的產業為旗幟。自由派方面，攝政的瑪麗亞·克里斯蒂娜以幼女王伊莎貝二世的名義執政，軍隊以五萬名正規軍與十萬名王室志願兵為骨架，但志願兵多數裝備簡陋、訓練不足，只能擔任守城與護送任務，實戰依賴少數職業部隊——埃斯帕特羅的北方軍、埃斯波·伊·米納率領的納瓦拉游擊隊，以及一八三五年後開赴戰場的外籍輔助軍團：英國輔助軍團、法國外國軍團、葡萄牙輔助師，另有數百名比利時與荷蘭志願兵。一八三四年四月，英、法、西、葡簽訂四國同盟，援助自由派並封鎖法境的武器與人員流入；卡洛斯派在葡萄牙一度得米格爾一世庇蔭，一八三四年後失去這個後方。自由派內部也分裂成「克里斯蒂諾斯」與「伊莎貝利諾斯」兩派，後來又有偏向溫和的莫雷迪亞政府，先後在抗戰、議和與換閣之間反覆，而卡洛斯派內部亦有卡洛斯五世與以蘇馬拉卡雷吉為首的巴斯克軍方之間的張力，軍方只肯為「維護舊制」而戰，並不願把王冠交到一個人手裡。
countriesEn: The two parties in this war were the Carlists and the Liberals. The Carlists held the rightful succession to be that of Carlos de Borbón, the late Ferdinand VII's brother, and in the north their armies went under the banner of the Hundred Thousand, forming with remarkable speed out of the resistance movement in Navarre, the three Basque provinces, Aragon and Catalonia. Their base was the parish priest and the village herdsman; their core strength came from fishermen, smugglers and farm bands who knew the coast and the mountain tracks, and their officers were largely infantry captains and veterans who had gone over from the liberal army. Their organisation kept the old battalion and company structure, supplemented by a guerrilla band in every village, known as the chapelgorris, the priest's blessing. The eastern theatre was run independently by Cabrera and the Count of Morella, active in the interior of Valencia and Catalonia. In the north the traditionalist support was concentrated in the rural districts of the Basque country and Navarre, rallying behind the fueros, the ancient constitutional privileges of those provinces, and the property of the Catholic church. On the liberal side the regent Maria Christina governed in the name of the child queen Isabella II. The liberal army rested on fifty thousand regulars and a hundred thousand royal volunteers, but the volunteers were badly equipped and poorly trained, fit only for the defence of towns and the escort of convoys; real fighting fell to a handful of professional formations, Espartero's Army of the North, Espoz y Mina's Navarrese guerrilla bands, and after 1835 the foreign auxiliary formations sent to the field, the British Auxiliary Legion, the French Foreign Legion and the Portuguese auxiliary division, together with several hundred Belgian and Dutch volunteers. In April 1834 Britain, France, Spain and Portugal signed the Quadruple Alliance, backing the liberals and closing the frontier against men and weapons reaching the Carlists; the Carlists had found shelter under Miguel I of Portugal and lost that refuge after 1834. The liberals themselves were split between the Cristinos and the Isabelinos, and later between the moderate party of the Moradia ministry, which moved in turn between fighting, negotiating and reshuffling cabinets, while inside the Carlist camp a tension ran between Carlos V and the Basque military leadership under Zumalacárregui, whose men would fight to keep the old order but would not hand the crown over to one man.
people: 關鍵人物分屬兩邊。卡洛斯一方：費爾南多七世之弟卡洛斯·德·波旁，一八三三年十月在維多利亞宣布自己為王（卡洛斯五世），他主持的一八三三年修道院還俗清單把大批教產推向拍賣，其中相當一部分後來落入卡洛斯派控制，成為其軍費與徵召的基礎；真正替他打北方的是巴斯克鄉村出身的老兵托馬斯·德·蘇馬拉卡雷吉，他一八三三年在納瓦拉拉起隊伍，一八三四年在阿拉瓦平原擊敗自由派，一八三五年包圍比斯凱時腿部中彈不治身亡；拉斐爾·馬羅托一八三九年代表卡洛斯在貝爾加拉與埃斯帕特羅簽下協議，隨即流亡倫敦；東線的拉蒙·卡布雷拉以「莫雷亞伯爵」之名活動，他一八三八年奪取莫雷亞與巴特亞，一八三七年率「王室遠征軍」打到馬德里城下。自由派一方：攝政的瑪麗亞·克里斯蒂娜掌政但少有軍事手腕；巴爾多梅羅·埃斯帕特羅是最重要的將領，他一八三五年在梅迪戈里亞擊敗蘇馬拉卡雷吉的後繼者，一八三六年盧查納一役解圍比斯凱，同年底占領維多利亞，一八四〇年親率大軍掃平馬埃斯特拉戈，同年出任攝政；弗朗西斯科·埃斯波·伊·米納是納瓦拉本地人，以游擊對游擊維持北線平衡；赫里莫·巴爾德斯、迪耶戈·德·萊昂、拉蒙·馬里亞·納爾瓦埃斯在東線與南部輪流指揮；「托雷諾」胡安·阿隆索·德·馬查多·莫拉洪在議會推動議和。一八三三年十一月，被推翻的前自由派將領托里霍斯等人在塞維利亞被公開處決，事件直接引發南方同情與響應，其慘烈形象在卡洛斯派文獻中被反覆引用。外籍方面：英國的德·萊西·埃文斯中校指揮英國輔助軍團，法國的約瑟夫·貝爾內爾指揮法國外國軍團，葡萄牙的安塔斯伯爵率葡軍師。宗教與地方一端，各地教區神甫是卡洛斯派最有效的後勤與情報管理者，北方由「牧人」加斯帕爾·德·豪雷吉以「神甫的祝福」小組維持村鎮戒備。
peopleEn: The decisive figures fall on two sides. On the Carlist side there was Carlos de Borbón, the brother of the late Ferdinand VII, who proclaimed himself king at Vitoria in October 1833 as Carlos V; the list of convents he put up for suppression in 1833 drove a great deal of church property to the auction block, and a considerable part of it later fell into Carlist hands, becoming the base of their war finance and of their levies. The man who really fought the north for him was a Basque soldier of fortune, Tomás de Zumalacárregui, who raised a force in Navarre in 1833, beat the liberals on the plains of Álava in 1834, and was wounded in the leg during the siege of Bilbao in 1835 and died of the wound; Rafael Maroto signed the agreement at Bergara in 1839 on Carlos's behalf and then went into exile in London; in the east Ramón Cabrera acted under the name of the Count of Morella, taking Morella and Batea in 1838 and leading the Royal Expedition of 1837 to the walls of Madrid. On the liberal side the regent Maria Christina held the government but showed little military judgement; Baldomero Espartero was the essential general, winning at Mendigorría in 1835 against Zumalacárregui's successor, relieving Biscay at Luchana in 1836, entering Vitoria at the end of that year, sweeping the Maestrazgo in 1840 with a great army and becoming regent in the same year; Francisco Espoz y Mina, a Navarrese by birth, kept the northern front balanced by fighting guerrilla with guerrilla; Jerónimo Valdés, Diego de León and Ramón María Narváez took turns in command in the east and the south; and Juan Alonso de Machado y Morahonda, the Toreno, pressed for negotiation in the Cortes. In November 1833 the former liberal officer Torrijos and his companions were publicly executed at Seville, an execution that drew immediate sympathy and revolt in the south and whose image was used again and again in Carlist writing. Among the foreigners, Lieutenant Colonel De Lacy Evans commanded the British Auxiliary Legion, Joseph Bernelle the French Foreign Legion, and the Count of Antas the Portuguese division. On the religious and local side the parish priests were the most effective administrators of Carlist supply and intelligence, and in the north Gaspar de Jáuregui, the Shepherd, kept the villages on a war footing with his bands of chapelgorris.
kits: 卡面這件輪發槍是最早的後膛手槍，十六世紀初在日耳曼與低地國家出現，機件昂貴，火藥仍須用火繩點燃，因此只配給火槍隊的軍官與衛兵。它同時屬於同一條技術譜系的末端：十六世紀的西班牙正是靠埃瓦爾、普拉森西亞、蒙德拉貢等巴斯克與納瓦拉一帶的鐵匠鋪，成批製造「火花槍」及其後膛手槍，賣給王室與海外軍隊。換句話說，卡面兵器的出生地，正是這場戰爭最慘烈的戰場。到一八三三年，輪發機件早已被燧發槍取代，火繩手槍更只餘古舊的收藏；自由派軍官與王室衛兵攜帶的是燧發的步槍手手槍（pistolas de pedrero），一八三〇年代後期開始流通雷管手槍，但數量極少，只配給高級指揮官與警衛連。卡洛斯派的手槍來源更雜，多數是繳獲的政府軍手槍與農家的獵槍，近距離交火中仍可一擊致命，軍官往往手槍與佩劍並用，維護上的麻煩在火藥而不在射速。除手槍外，雙方步兵主力仍是滑膛燧發火槍與刺刀，騎兵與炮兵用短管卡賓槍，炮兵配備四磅、六磅、八磅與十二磅野戰炮及臼炮；卡洛斯派全境火炮極少，多為繳獲品，藏於山村與修道院，靠夜襲奪取。雙方都有大量王室志願兵，但多數只有獵槍、火繩短槍，甚至削尖的長矛與農具。交通上，卡洛斯派依賴騾隊、人力背運與少量牛車，能走山徑小道；自由派依賴大車隊與主要谷道，糧秣與彈藥由船運至比斯開沿岸再轉內陸，前線車隊必須有騎兵護送，否則常在途中被截斷。卡洛斯派在村落中就地徵發糧食、牲畜與鞋料，這種自養式後勤是他們能以少量骨幹拖住大軍的關鍵。穿衣上，卡洛斯山民以粗呢「卡巴尼亞」披風兼作雨衣與睡袋，頭戴黑色闊邊帽，是其最鮮明的形象；而正是製造過十六世紀輪發手槍的巴斯克鐵匠，在一八三〇年代仍為卡洛斯軍官打造新的燧發手槍——同樣的手藝，不同的年代。
kitsEn: The wheellock pistol on this card is the earliest breech-loaded pistol, appearing in the German lands and the Low Countries in the early sixteenth century. Its mechanism was costly and the charge still had to be set off with a match, so it was issued only to the officers and guards of the arquebusiers. At the same time it sits at the end of a technical line: the Spanish state of the sixteenth century bought its guns in bulk from the smithies of Eibar, Plasencia, Mondragón and the Basque and Navarrese districts around them, where escopetas de chispa and their pistol versions were made for the crown and for foreign armies. In other words, the birthplace of the weapon on the card is the very battlefield on which this war was fought hardest. By 1833 the wheellock had long been superseded by the flintlock and the matchlock survived only as an antique; liberal officers and the royal guard carried flintlock pistols, the pistolas de pedrero, and percussion pistols only began to appear late in the 1830s in tiny numbers, for senior commanders and the guard companies alone. The Carlists had a more mixed supply, mostly captured government pistols and farm shotguns, still lethal at close range, and their officers wore pistol and sabre together, the difficulty lying in the powder rather than the rate of fire. Beyond the pistol, the infantry of both sides remained smoothbore flintlock muskets with bayonets, cavalry and artillery used short carbines, and the artillery park held four-, six-, eight- and twelve-pounder field guns with howitzers. The Carlists had very few guns for the whole country, mostly captured pieces hidden in mountain villages and monasteries and taken back in night attacks. Both sides had large numbers of royal volunteers, but most of them had only shotguns, short matchlock muskets, or even sharpened stakes and farm tools. In transport the Carlists relied on mule trains, men's backs and a few ox-carts, and could use the mountain tracks; the liberals relied on great wagon trains on the main valleys, with powder and grain landed by sea on the Biscay coast and carried inland, and their columns had to be escorted by cavalry or they were cut up on the road. The Carlists levied grain, cattle and footwear in the villages on the spot, and that self-supporting supply was what allowed a small hard core to pin down large armies. In dress the Carlist mountaineer wore a coarse cloak, the cabaña, as raincoat and blanket together, with a broad black hat, the most vivid image of the movement; and the Basque smiths who had made sixteenth-century wheellock pistols were still making new flintlock pistols for Carlist officers in the 1830s, the same craft in a different age.
tactics: 卡洛斯派的打法是典型的地方性游擊戰：村鎮民兵白天耕作、夜間集合，接到警號即在指定時限內集結，由村鎮書吏、牧人與走私者擔任嚮導與情報，以熟悉的小徑接近目標，在黎明前以一次齊射衝擊敵軍宿營或護送隊，隨即散入山中。他們極少接受會戰，除非能確保以多打少或對方彈藥耗盡；一八三五年末至三六年的比斯凱與巴斯克南部戰線，正是這種累積的壓力迫使自由派改以遠征而非會戰去解決問題。北方總部設在緊鄰埃斯特利亞的阿梅斯科阿斯，位於潘普洛納與維多利亞之間的布倫達河谷，夾在烏爾瓦薩山與安迪亞山之間，退路縱橫；一八三五年一月卡洛斯派奪取巴斯特安，靠的正是這些山徑與地方耳目。卡洛斯派在情報上佔優：地方支持網與間諜使其得以用快捷的「閃電急信」在多個山頭之間傳遞命令，自由派軍隊只能在谷地行軍，資訊與補給都慢一步；卡布雷拉還常驅趕牛群製造假足跡，或佯作側翼展開以誘敵深入。卡洛斯派的主要打擊目標是糧秣與信用：切斷車隊、襲擊護送、奪取地方稅收、破壞村鎮中的徵兵與物資點，用這種辦法把自由派遠征軍拖入無補給的消耗戰；一八三六年十二月埃斯帕特羅在巴爾馬塞達受挫，即是此種戰法的成果。自由派則以炮兵、圍城與封鎖對付卡洛斯派：一八三五年進攻比斯凱，一八三六年盧查納解圍並占領維多利亞，一八三八年南下掃平莫雷亞與巴特亞，一八四〇年再以縱隊追入馬埃斯特拉戈。圍城需要工程器材與持續糧道，這正是自由派最弱的一環；莫雷亞的圍城延續數月，最後由守軍在彈藥告罄後開門投降。外籍輔助軍團在攻堅中表現突出，但缺乏山地經驗，一八三七年九月安多因一役後便再無力擔任突擊。俘虜與傷員問題上，雙方截然不同：一八三五年英國艾略特勛爵的調解促成雙方同意不殺俘虜、定期交換並保護傷員，協議先在巴斯克地區施行，但未經審判的槍決仍時有發生，這也是卡洛斯派在文獻中自詡為「為教會與王位而戰」的道德訴求所在。
tacticsEn: The Carlist way of war was local guerrilla fighting: village militia tilled by day and assembled at night, coming together within a fixed time when the alarm was given, with village scribes, herdsmen and smugglers serving as guides and intelligence, approaching along the tracks they knew and striking at dawn with a single volley against an enemy camp or an escorted convoy before dispersing into the hills. They would seldom accept a general engagement unless they could be sure of superior numbers or of an enemy out of ammunition, and it was this cumulative pressure in Biscay and the southern Basque country in 1835 and 1836 that forced the liberals to answer with expeditions rather than battles. The northern headquarters stood at the Améscoas, next to Estella, in the Burunda valley between Pamplona and Vitoria, wedged between the Urbasa and Andía ranges with escape routes in every direction; the Carlist seizure of Baztán in January 1835 was made along exactly these tracks and with exactly these local eyes. On intelligence the Carlists held the advantage: their local support network and spies let them pass swift flash messages between hilltops, while liberal columns had to march in the valleys and were a step behind in both information and supply, and Cabrera often drove herds of cattle to leave false tracks or feigned a flank to draw the enemy in. The Carlist target was supply and credit: cutting convoys, raiding escorts, seizing local tax and destroying the recruiting and collecting points of the villages, and so dragging liberal expeditionary columns into an attritional war they could not supply; the defeat of Espartero at Balmaseda in December 1836 was the fruit of that method. The liberals answered with artillery, siege and blockade: the attack on Bilbao in 1835, the relief of the Biscay capital and the entry into Vitoria in 1836, the sweep through Morella and Batea in 1838, and the drive into the Maestrazgo in 1840. Siege demanded engineers and a continuous line of supply, which was precisely the liberal weakness; the siege of Morella dragged on for months and ended when the garrison, out of powder, opened the gates. The foreign auxiliary formations did well in the assault but had no experience of the mountains, and after Andoain in September 1837 they were no longer fit for the role of shock troops. On prisoners and wounded the two sides differed sharply: in 1835 the mission of the British Lord Eliot brought both to agree not to kill prisoners, to exchange them regularly and to respect the wounded, an agreement applied first in the Basque country, though executions without trial continued from time to time, and it was this that the Carlists invoked in their literature when they claimed to be fighting for the church and the crown.
data: 可核對的數字如下。戰爭自一八三三年九月二十九日費爾南多七世去世起算，至一八四〇年七月六日結束，前後約六年九個月，是十九世紀歐洲規模最大、死亡最重的內戰，交戰兵力超過半島戰爭。一八三三年西班牙人口約一千二百三十萬，全國人口密度每平方公里僅二十餘人。自由派方面全戰動員約五十萬人，另有外籍志願兵一萬八千餘人，其中法軍損失約七千七百人、英軍約二千五百人、葡軍五十人；一八三三年西班牙軍力為五萬正規軍與十萬王室志願兵，另有六百五十二名將官。雙方軍人傷亡的估計差距極大：自由派常被引為一萬五千至六萬五千人，卡洛斯派為一萬五千至六萬人。會戰的紀年序列相當清楚：一八三四年五月阿爾薩蘇阿（二十二日）、古利納（六月十八日）、阿拉維亞的歡樂之役（十月二十七日）、埃查瓦里出售站（十月二十八日）、門達薩（十二月十二日）；一八三五年阿爾塔薩（四月二十二日）、梅迪戈里亞（七月十六日，自由派決定性勝利）；一八三六年阿爾拉班（一月十六至十八日）、維利亞爾羅夫萊多（九月二十日）、馬哈塞特（十一月二十三日）、盧查納（十二月二十四日）；一八三七年奧里亞門迪（三月十六日）、伊倫（五月十七日）、安多因（九月十四日）、阿蘭蘇埃克（九月）、雷圖埃爾塔（十月四日，王室遠征軍的終點）；一八三八年莫雷亞（五月十三日）、佩納塞拉達（六月二十日至二十二日）、馬埃拉（十月一日）；一八三九年拉馬萊斯（五月十三日）。戰地醫療的記錄同樣殘酷：一八三八年莫雷亞戰役中，自由派傷兵有約四分之三在數日內不治。各次會戰的確切兵力，各家史家估計相差數倍，卡洛斯派報數向來偏高，因此此處只列有明確紀年的戰役，而不引用單方自報的兵力。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked run as follows. The war is counted from the death of Ferdinand VII on 29 September 1833 and ended on 6 July 1840, roughly six years and nine months, and was the largest and deadliest civil war in nineteenth-century Europe, fought by more men than the Peninsular War. Spain had about 12.3 million inhabitants in 1833 and a density of only a little over twenty to the square kilometre. The liberal side mobilised about five hundred thousand men over the whole war, with more than eighteen thousand foreign volunteers besides, of whom the French lost about 7,700, the British about 2,500 and the Portuguese fifty; the Spanish forces in 1833 were fifty thousand regulars and a hundred thousand royal volunteers, with six hundred and fifty-two general officers. The estimates of military casualties differ enormously, the liberals commonly being given as between fifteen thousand and sixty-five thousand and the Carlists between fifteen thousand and sixty thousand. The chronology of engagements is comparatively clear: Alsasua on 22 April 1834, Gulina on 18 June, Alegría de Álava on 27 October, Venta de Echávarri on 28 October and Mendaza on 12 December; Artaza on 22 April 1835 and Mendigorría on 16 July, a decisive liberal victory; Arlabán from 16 to 18 January 1836, Villarrobledo on 20 September, Majaceite on 23 November and Luchana on 24 December; Oriamendi on 16 March 1837, Irún on 17 May, Andoain on 14 September, Aranzueque in September and Retuerta on 4 October, the end of the Royal Expedition; Morella on 13 May 1838, Peñacerrada from 20 to 22 June and Maella on 1 October; and Ramales on 13 May 1839. The medical record is just as bleak: in the Morella campaign of 1838 about three quarters of the liberal wounded died within days of being hit. Exact strengths for any single engagement vary by a factor of several between historians, and the Carlist figures are always pitched high, so only engagements with firm dates are listed here and no self-reported strengths are quoted.
cause: 起因是多層的。第一層是王位：一八三〇年費爾南多七世廢止一八一二年的王位繼承法規章，使西班牙的繼承秩序失去文字依據；他在一八三三年九月二十九日病逝，留下年僅三歲的女兒伊莎貝二世與薩伏依出身的攝政的瑪麗亞·克里斯蒂娜。卡洛斯派主張王冠應沿父系男嗣傳給費爾南多之弟，並主張攝政與未成年君主制違背西班牙舊制；自由派則堅持君權須有憲章與議會限制。第二層是教會與產業：一八三三年由卡洛斯主持的修道院還俗清單把大批教產推向拍賣，天主教會在北部山區的庇護院、醫院與牧區岌岌可危，傳統主義者斷言教產一旦被吞，聖職與聖禮都會隨之消亡。第三層是地方特權：自由派政府推行全國一致的兵役與法制，巴斯克與納瓦拉的「福爾羅斯」正是要在這上面讓步，而執法人員與新稅在鄉村的推行，把整片山區的農莊與教區推到了卡洛斯一方。第四層是直接導火線：一八三三年十月卡洛斯在維多利亞宣布為王，北方隨即在納瓦拉、阿拉瓦、比斯凱同時起事；十一月被推翻的前自由派將領托里霍斯等人在塞維利亞被公開處決，成為全國性的騷動，也成了卡洛斯派宣傳的素材；其後自由派在加泰隆尼亞與瓦倫西亞的清剿把抵抗推向東線，使原本互不相干的三處起義連成一場內戰。此外，國家財政在美洲殖民地崩潰後已近枯竭，一八二四至三三年年均收入不足戰前的一半，持久戰對雙方都意味著更長的飢餓與更多的散兵；一八三四年四國同盟帶來的外援與封鎖，又把戰爭的方向推向了北方山區。
causeEn: The causes ran in several layers. The first was the crown. In 1830 Ferdinand VII revoked the Pragmatic Sanction of 1812, so that the succession order of Spain lost its written basis; he died on 29 September 1833, leaving a daughter of three, Isabella II, and a regent from Savoy, Maria Christina. The Carlists held that the crown should pass along the male line of the father's house to Ferdinand's brother, and that a regency over a child monarch violated the old customs of Spain, while the liberals insisted that royal power must be limited by a charter and a legislature. The second was the church and its property: the list of convents for suppression drawn up under Carlos's own authority in 1833 drove a great deal of church land to the auction block, and the hospitals, refuges and parishes of the northern mountains felt their institutions to be in danger, the traditionalists arguing that if the property were swallowed the offices and the sacraments would go with it. The third was provincial privilege: the liberal government pressed a uniform conscription and a uniform legal order, the fueros of the Basque provinces and of Navarre were exactly what the Carlists wanted conceded, and the presence of officials and of new taxes in the villages drove the farming population and the parishes of the whole mountain region into the Carlist camp. The fourth was the immediate occasion: in October 1833 Carlos proclaimed himself king at Vitoria and the north rose at once in Navarre, Álava and Biscay; in November the fallen liberal officer Torrijos and his companions were publicly executed at Seville, a national shock and a ready-made subject for Carlist propaganda; and the subsequent Liberal suppression in Catalonia and Valencia pushed the resistance eastward, welding three unrelated risings into a single civil war. Beyond all this the treasury was empty after the loss of the American colonies, the average annual income between 1824 and 1833 being barely more than half the pre-war level, so that a war of endurance meant longer hunger and more stragglers for both sides, and the foreign aid and frontier closure brought by the Quadruple Alliance of 1834 pushed the war towards the mountains of the north.
impact: 影響在制度上最為持久。這場戰爭第一次把巴斯克與納瓦拉的「福爾羅斯」推到西班牙國家政治的爭議中心：一八三八年馬德里與卡洛斯派溫和派訂下的「和平與福爾羅斯」方案，把古老特權以國家承認的形式固定下來，同年頒布的敕令確認了巴斯克三省與納瓦拉的特權並豁免其兵役，使這些省在往後數十年裡幾乎不向中央提供常備兵源。一八三九年八月三十一日貝爾加拉的「擁抱」以協議收束北方戰事，卻也讓卡洛斯一系的王位主張繼續存在——卡洛斯五世流亡國外後，姪子相繼以卡洛斯六世、七世的名號發動第二次與第三次卡洛斯戰爭，直到一八七六年才被制憲會議徹底否定。埃斯帕特羅一八四〇年出任攝政後，一八四一年一度下令取消這些特權，引發北部軍民反抗，最終在一八四四年他自己下台時被一併恢復，自由派此後轉向溫和，長達二十年的「溫和年代」由此開始，而它同時也意味著卡洛斯問題被擱置而非解決。在軍事史上，這場戰爭被視為前工業時代歐洲最後一場大規模的總體戰：交戰人數超過半島戰爭，手段卻以游擊、圍城、封鎖與徵召民兵為主，幾乎沒有決定性會戰，它提供的大量游擊對正規軍的實例，在後來的戰爭研究中被反覆引用。西班牙史學也因這場戰爭而長期偏斜，官方曾大力扶植傳統主義者的著作，使這段歷史至今仍有不同的版本。政治上，不少研究者把這場戰爭視為「兩個西班牙」觀念的源頭：同一片國土、同一支軍隊被分成互相否定的一邊，這一分裂在七十年後的內戰中再次上演。財政後果極重：殖民地早已盡失，戰爭又耗盡國庫，自由派不得不更多地倚賴英國金融家的貸款與英國的海上支持，這條依賴線在往後半個世紀裡一直延伸。
impactEn: The consequences are most durable on the institutional side. This war put the fueros of the Basque country and of Navarre for the first time at the centre of Spanish national politics: the Peace and Fueros arrangement concluded in Madrid in 1838 between the government and the moderate Carlists fixed those ancient privileges in the form of a state recognition, and the decree issued in the same year confirmed the privileges of the three Basque provinces and of Navarre and exempted them from conscription, so that for decades afterwards those provinces supplied the centre with almost no regular troops. The Embrace of Bergara on 31 August 1839 closed the northern fighting by agreement, but left the dynastic claim of the Carlists alive: after Carlos V went into exile his nephews in turn raised the Second and Third Carlist Wars under the names Carlos VI and Carlos VII, and the claim was not finally negated until 1876. When Espartero became regent in 1840 he attempted in 1841 to abolish those privileges, the northern districts rose, and the privileges were restored when he fell from power in 1844; the liberals then turned moderate and the two long decades of the Década Moderada began, which also meant that the Carlist question was set aside rather than settled. In military history the war is treated as the last great general conflict of the pre-industrial age in Europe: more men were engaged than in the Peninsular War, yet the means were guerrilla action, siege, blockade and levied militia, and there was hardly a decisive engagement; the mass of examples it left of irregular war against regular troops has been cited again and again in later study of war. Spanish historiography has been long skewed by the conflict, the official sponsorship of traditionalist scholarship having produced different versions of the same history down to the present. Politically many writers see the war as the seed of the idea of the two Spains, one country and one army split into halves that denied each other, a division that was acted out again seventy years later in the civil war. The financial cost was heavy: the colonies were long gone, the war emptied the treasury again, and the liberals came to lean harder on loans from British financiers and on British sea power, a line of dependence that ran on for the rest of the century.
result: 結果是自由派贏得王位與國家，但多數戰場並非靠會戰取得。北方自一八三五年起由蘇馬拉卡雷吉主導，佔據巴斯克與納瓦拉的山區；一八三五年四月英國艾略特勛爵的調解使雙方同意不殺俘虜、定期交換並保護傷員，協議先在巴斯克施行，戰爭的野蠻程度因此下降；同年六月蘇馬拉卡雷吉在比斯凱受傷不治，七月梅迪戈里亞一役自由派得勝，北方遂再無能與之抗衡的統一指揮。一八三六年十二月埃斯帕特羅在巴爾馬塞達受挫，一八三七年一月的阿爾拉班與三月十六日的奧里亞門迪仍由卡洛斯派得手，同年九月十四日的安多因之後，英國輔助軍團便不再能發揮突擊作用；該年七月的「王室遠征軍」雖一度打到馬德里城下，卻在阿蘭蘇埃克與雷圖埃爾塔一帶被擊退，卡洛斯派自此再無力把戰爭帶進卡斯蒂利亞。東線是自由派最後攻克的戰場：一八三八年五月卡布雷拉奪取莫雷亞與巴特亞，兵力一度推進到瓦倫西亞平原並圍困薩貢托，同年十月一日馬埃拉之役卡洛斯派再度得手；但自由派在佩納塞拉達（一八三八年六月）與拉馬萊斯（一八三九年五月）相繼得手，一八四〇年五月三十日莫雷亞重新回到自由派之手，埃斯帕特羅的縱隊深入馬埃斯特拉戈，卡洛斯派主力退入法境，到一八四〇年七月六日戰爭實際結束。和約的實質是：北方以貝爾加拉協議換得特權與兵役豁免，卡洛斯五世的王位主張被擱置但未廢除，卡洛斯一系退入法國境內從事下一輪活動。卡面那件輪發手槍也隨之退場——它在一八三三年早已被燧發手槍取代，只在軍官與衛兵手上留了一個象徵性的位置；真正決定這場戰爭勝負的，是步槍的射程、炮兵的分量、山徑的走向、車隊的安全，還有海權與外交這兩樣更靠後的東西。
resultEn: The result was a liberal victory in the crown and in the state, though few of the battlefields were decided in the field. In the north the war was led from 1833 by Zumalacárregui, who held the Basque and Navarrese mountains; in April 1835 the mission of the British Lord Eliot brought both sides to agree not to kill prisoners, to exchange them regularly and to respect the wounded, the agreement applying first in the Basque country, and the savagery of the war diminished accordingly. In June 1835 Zumalacárregui was wounded at Bilbao and died of it, and the liberal victory at Mendigorría in July left the north without the single commander able to match the free government. Espartero was checked at Balmaseda in December 1836, and the Carlists still won at Arlabán in January 1837 and at Oriamendi on 16 March; after Andoain on 14 September the British Auxiliary Legion was no longer able to function as a shock force. The Royal Expedition of July 1837 reached the walls of Madrid but was driven back around Aranzueque and Retuerta, and the Carlists never again carried the war into Castile. The east was the last theatre the liberals conquered: in May 1838 Cabrera took Morella and Batea, drove his men out on to the plain of Valencia and besieged Sagunto, and won again at Maella on 1 October; but the liberal side took Peñacerrada in June 1838 and Ramales on 13 May 1839, Morella returned to Madrid's hands on 30 May 1840, Espartero's columns drove deep into the Maestrazgo and the Carlist main body withdrew into France, and by 6 July 1840 the war was over in all but name. The substance of the settlement was this: in the north an agreement at Bergara bought the privileges and the exemption from conscription, the Carlist claim to the crown was set aside but not abolished, and the Carlist line retired into France to prepare the next round. The wheellock pistol on the card retired with the rest: by 1833 it had long been replaced by the flintlock pistol and kept only a symbolic place in the hands of officers and guards. What really decided the war was the reach of the musket, the weight of the artillery, the line of the mountain tracks, the safety of the convoys, and, later in the order of things, sea power and diplomacy.
